answers.how: A quadratic fit to the ball trajectory gives vertical acceleration ≈555 px/s², establishing 1.766 cm/px. The ball diameter is ≈12.5 px, giving 22.1 cm.
The middle person's head-to-foot height is ≈98.5 px. Using the gravity-derived scale of 1.766 cm/px gives ≈174 cm.
In the later upright frames, the passer measures ≈85.5 px head to foot. Multiplying by 1.766 cm/px gives ≈151 cm.
The receiver measures ≈99 px head to foot near the start. At 1.766 cm/px, this is ≈175 cm.
The initial horizontal separation between the players is approximately 249 px. The gravity-derived scale, 0.01766 m/px, gives ≈4.4 m.
At 1.00 s, the fitted trajectory gives horizontal and vertical velocities of approximately 114 and 163 px/s. Their magnitude times 0.01766 m/px is ≈3.51 m/s.
The ball's horizontal position changes at an average ≈112 px/s. Multiplying by the gravity-derived scale of 0.01766 m/px gives ≈1.98 m/s.
